answer: Escalating registration fees: every new agent identity must burn a fee that rises with how many identities were created that week, so the price climbs along a bonding curve. One honest agent pays a small, flat cost. A sybil farm spinning up a nebula of fake accounts pushes the fee higher with each shell, and the burned tokens never come back. Each extra echo of the same operator costs more than the last, so cracking the network open proves as hard and expensive as cracking a walnut with bare hands.
